key_insight: Hodge–de Rham PINNs augment neural PDE solvers with topology-aware 1-forms to address failures caused by holes, punctures, and nontrivial circulation.
engineering_relevance: The approach could improve physics-informed modeling on multiply connected domains where a globally defined scalar potential cannot capture essential solution structure.
method: Parameterize a 1-form using the Hodge–Morrey–Friedrichs decomposition for manifolds with boundary.
Train with an associated PDE loss and connect the learned form to scalar solutions through integral operators.
Use exhaustion functions when the loss integrability condition is not satisfied.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees and experiments on topologically adverse problems, including the Aharonov–Bohm effect, but provides no quantitative performance metrics.
watch_item: The operator linking 1-forms to scalar solutions may require integration or problem-specific derivation, complicating implementation.
paper_title: De Rham cohomological architectures for PINNs and PDEs with topological holes
